scope: Full3file code read; no new test executed by root and no P0 launched. Existing child test result pending; findings are source-inspection not behavioral proof.

findings.finding: Writable /output directory has no enforced aggregate disk cap while code runs. max_output_bytes is checked after exit and tmpfs cap applies only to /tmp. Arbitrary code can fill host output directory with many/huge files for1200s.
findings.needed: Bound actual writable output during execution. Prefer exact precreated single prediction-file bind with no writable host directory and enforced per-file RLIMIT_FSIZE; adapt entry to write that sole file, preserve strict output semantics. Or measured quota/tmpfs+trusted extraction alternative. Need below/above actual disk-cap and sibling-file-write negative tests.

findings.finding: _cleanup_container swallows errors and does not verify absence; exception paths process.kill may not reap. SIGTERM/session loss/outer cancellation has no handler so native ORX PGID cancellation can leave named Docker child. success can be published after unproven cleanup.
findings.needed: Handle trusted SIGTERM/abort/timeouts using existing runner process (not new supervisor), reap bounded child, verify exact container absence, return CLEANUP_UNCONFIRMED/blocked if uncertain. Tests actual interrupt/TERM/client loss plus exact-name absence; no daemon-global cleanup.

findings.finding: _prepare_output chmods arbitrary trusted parent to0711 before symlink/type check, widens existing directory; comment says0700but actual0711. Input hash read and feature/output parsing reopen path unsafely and may consume unbounded changed file. max_bytes argument unused in _read_feature_ids.
findings.needed: Reject output parent symlink before any chmod; no mutation of existing unrelated parent permissions. Open exact regular nofollow+nonblock, enforce limits during reads, fstat before/after, parse/hash same bounded bytes. Output bytes hash must correspond to bytes parsed, not second read.

findings.finding: Network test connects to127.0.0.1:9 with no server, so weak network would also pass. Unmounted secret test checks path never mounted in control and unset env that is never injected. Memory test accepts TIMEOUT so does not demonstrate memory enforcement. Wrong-order named test only hasNaN. test_failing_first_missing_runner_import is a constant assertion.
findings.needed: Failing-first actual canary endpoints/paths, explicit environment sentinel supplied only weak control, measured cgroup memory/pids event or separate memory-failure evidence, actual wrong-order mutation and cleanup checks. Remove/relabel fake failing-first name; record uncovered Tcases honestly.

findings.finding: _RUN_ID_RE only UUIDv4. ORX may not contractually guarantee v4; config permits bool/NaN in numeric fields. Docker executable is PATH-derived and container_entry is module-relative mutable closure.
findings.needed: Root will map native ORX run ID only; accept canonical UUID identity without guessing v4, exact type finite bounds. Bind trusted docker executable/entry source in root deployment and rederive installed source posthash; do not claim identity from command strings alone.

findings.finding: Generated module can monkeypatch pandas/builtins/host entry logic inside container; treat entry as formatting convenience only, not trusted validation of arbitrary code. Infinity iterable list can fill memory but container cap handles it.
findings.needed: Final trust resides in host byte parser/scorer using original feature IDs. Preserve this in scope. Independent host parser must reject wrong IDs/nonfinite/extra columns, even if generated code overwrites output directly.
